The most interesting number in our entire dataset belongs to this brand. The Remington Ceramic Ionic carries 48,228 Canadian ratings at 4.4★ — the largest review base of any hair dryer we track, ahead of the wavytalk 1875W’s 32,950 and the slopehill 1902’s 22,195.

And it sells roughly 319 units a month. For comparison, the slopehill 1902 moves about 8,660 at BSR #1, the wavytalk about 2,948, and the Remington sits at BSR #9 with 319 Amazon.ca data.

That gap is the story of this brand, and it is worth understanding before you buy — because it tells you something about how Remington dryers are actually sold, which is not how most of this category is sold.

Why Remington has 48,228 ratings but only 319 units a month

This is what a legacy listing looks like, and the pattern is worth unpacking because it is easy to misread.

MetricCeramic IonicSlopehill 1902Wavytalk 1875W
Ratings count48,22822,19532,950
Est. units/month3198,6602,948
Category BSR913
Days on sale1,959 (~5.4 yr)1,153 (~3.2 yr)1,716 (~4.7 yr)

Reviews accumulate; sales velocity does not. A product on sale for 5.4 years collects ratings the whole time, so a long-lived listing carries a large cumulative total even when its current monthly volume is modest. The slopehill, by contrast, has been on sale for 3.2 years, has half the ratings, and outsells the Remington by roughly 27×.

What that means practically. A huge ratings count tells you the product has been around a long time and that most buyers were satisfied. It does not tell you the product is currently in demand, currently well-stocked, or currently the best option at its price. Those are different questions.

The second signal in the same data. Our keyword research shows only about ten searches a month in Canada for Remington hair dryer terms. Yet the products sell steadily. That combination points to shelf-driven purchasing — people buying in Walmart Canada, Canadian Tire or similar, not researching online first.

Why that matters to you. If you are reading this, you are in the minority who researches. The 4.4–4.5★ ratings are real and the sample is large, but you have access to information the typical Remington buyer did not, and it is worth using — see the comparison further down.

Remington hair dryer models compared

Two Canadian models, both conventional, both budget.

1. Remington Ceramic Ionic — the long-lived volume listing

about C$28 · 4.4★ (48,228 ratings) · about 319 units/month · BSR #9 · 5.4 years on sale · Buy Box: Amazon (1 seller)

What we liked

  • 48,228 ratings at 4.4★ — the largest review base in our dataset, so the rating is as stable as a rating can be Amazon.ca data
  • 5.4 years on sale, the second-longest track record we track Amazon.ca data
  • Ceramic ionic — a real material property on the element, plus the feature with the best record in our data at 17% negative (manufacturer claim, review analysis)
  • about C$28 — among the cheapest dryers we track Amazon.ca data

What we didn’t

  • Budget band, where our data shows a 30.3% complaint rate across 3,259 reviews, against 9.6% over C$120 Review analysis

  • One seller with Amazon holding the Buy Box, so no brand-operated storefront Amazon.ca data
  • Conventional, not brushless Manufacturer claim

Skip if: your hair is thick or long — airflow is the limitation.

Is Remington a reliable brand?

The honest read: it is a long-established value brand competing in the band our data flags.

What Remington brings:

FactorAssessment
Largest review base in our dataset48,228 ratings at 4.4★ on the Ceramic Ionic
LongevityUp to 5.4 years on sale
Priceabout C$26–28.49
DistributionWidely available in Canadian physical retail
Motor technologyConventional, not brushless
Buy Box holderAmazon on both — no brand storefront
Price bandUnder C$50 → 30.3% complaint rate

The band is the caveat, and it applies to both models. Our data shows 30.3% complaint rate under C$50 across 3,259 reviews, against 9.6% over C$120 across 334, and the median reported failure across the category is 5.5 months Review analysis.

What we cannot tell you. Whether either Remington model is more or less reliable than its band average. The 48,228-rating sample is large enough that its 4.4★ is meaningful, but star ratings and complaint rates measure different things — a buyer who gives three stars for “fine for the price” is not the same signal as a one-star failure report.

Practical guidance for both: check the ALCI plug for its rectangular GFCI-style box on arrival, and check the cord strain relief where it enters the handle. Cord and connector failure accounted for 417 mentions in our dataset, second only to complete stoppage at 601 — see how long hair dryers actually last.

Who should buy a Remington hair dryer

Buy one if:

  • Your budget is under C$30 and you want a long-established brand rather than an unknown listing
  • You want the largest evidence base available at this price — 48,228 ratings is not a small sample
  • Your hair is short to medium and not especially thick
  • You are buying in person at Walmart Canada or Canadian Tire and want to compare by hand

Do not buy one if:

  • Your hair is thick or long — you want airflow, and both models are conventional (see thick hair)
  • You want a brand-operated listing and one clear warranty counterparty
  • You need dual voltage for travel
  • You can stretch to about C$100 — the complaint rate roughly thirds at that threshold

Remington hair dryer FAQ

Is Remington a good hair dryer brand? It is a long-established value brand and both Canadian models we track sit in the budget band. The Ceramic Ionic carries 48,228 ratings at 4.4 stars, the largest review base in our entire dataset, and the Damage Protection model rates 4.5 stars from 806 ratings.

Why does the Remington Ceramic Ionic have 48,228 ratings but low sales? It is what a legacy listing looks like. Reviews accumulate over years, so a long-lived product carries a large total even when current velocity is modest. At roughly 319 units a month against 48,228 ratings, it has been on sale for about 5.4 years. High total ratings do not indicate high current demand.

Where do people usually buy Remington hair dryers? Mostly in physical retail rather than through search. Our keyword data shows only about ten searches a month for Remington hair dryer terms in Canada, while the products sell steadily in our sales data. That pattern — high sales, negligible search volume — points to shelf-driven purchasing in stores such as Walmart Canada and Canadian Tire.

Are Remington hair dryers dual voltage? Neither of the two Canadian models we track is marketed as dual voltage, so treat them as home dryers. Voltage was the single most-discussed topic in our entire dataset at 785 mentions. For travel, see our travel hair dryer guide.

Is Remington good for fine hair? Partly. Both models sit in the budget band where our data shows a 30.3% complaint rate, which is the main caveat. On the plus side, the Damage Protection model is explicitly positioned around reduced heat damage, which is the right concern for fine hair — see our fine hair guide.

How long does a Remington hair dryer last? We cannot say specifically. Across 8,261 Canadian reviews the median reported failure was 5.5 months, and dryers under C$50 had a 30.3% complaint rate against 9.6% over C$120. Both Remington models sit in the under-C$50 band.

Our verdict on Remington hair dryers

A long-established value brand with the largest evidence base in our dataset — and the same budget-band caveat as every competitor at this price.

Buy the Damage Protection at about C$26 if you want the currently active listing — 4.5★ from 806 ratings, roughly 536 units a month at BSR #6, and a positioning around reduced heat damage that suits fine or heat-sensitive hair.

Buy the Ceramic Ionic at about C$28 if the 48,228-rating sample matters more to you — it is the largest in our dataset and the rating is stable. Just understand that a huge cumulative total reflects a long listing life, not current demand: 319 units a month against the slopehill’s 8,660.

Both sit in the under-C$50 band where our data shows a 30.3% complaint rate, against 9.6% over C$120. That is the honest trade at this price — and if you can stretch to about C$100, our best hair dryers under C$150 covers what that extra money actually buys.
